done

echo

echo
echo "=== any compiler errors/warnings on our files? ==="

input.description: Independently verify the built image and report tree state
input.command:
cd /home/czp/openvela_contest
O=cmake_out/remote-ctrl-verify

echo "=== image ==="
ls -la $O/nuttx | awk '{printf "  %s  %s bytes  %s %s %s\n", $9, $5, $6, $7, $8}'
echo "  built at: $(date -r $O/nuttx '+%F %T')"
echo

echo "=== config flag in the ACTUAL built .config ==="
grep -n 'CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REMOTE_CTRL' $O/.config || echo "  MISSING"
echo

echo "=== our 6 objects, with sizes ==="
find $O -path '*ai_agent*' \( -name 'remote_*.c.o' -o -name 'tool_remote_agent.c.o' \) | sort | while read -r f; do
  printf '  %7d  %s\n' "$(stat -c%s "$f")" "${f#$O/}"
done
echo

echo "=== markers inside the ELF (strings cached once, no pipefail trap) ==="
S=$(mktemp); strings $O/nuttx > "$S"
for m in remote_agent_prompt remote_agent_status set_remote_auth remote_deny remote_once 'device-to-bridge' 'bridge-to-device' 'remote-ctrl-'; do
  printf '  %-22s %s\n' "$m" "$(grep -cF "$m" "$S") hit(s)"
done
rm -f "$S"
echo

echo "=== TREE STATE RIGHT NOW (build stages files; 'down' restores) ==="
printf '  staged into packages/ai_agent : %s files\n' "$(git -C packages/ai_agent status --porcelain | wc -l)"
D=vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/defconfig
printf '  defconfig feature flag        : %s\n' "$(grep -c 'CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REMOTE_CTRL' $D) 处"
printf '  defconfig backup kept         : %s\n' "$([ -f $HOME/.remote-ctrl-demo/defconfig.orig ] && echo yes || echo NO)"
echo "  diff vs pre-work backup (应只有 1 行新增):"
diff "$HOME/rc_defconfig_orig.bak" "$D" | sed 's/^/    /'

# The openvela root is found by walking up for its marker layout rather than by
# counting levels, so this script works from tools/acp-bridge/bin, from
# packages/ai_agent/scripts, or from a worktree — wherever it is checked in.
find_root() {
  local d="$1"
  while [ "$d" != "/" ]; do
    if [ -d "$d/nuttx" ] && [ -d "$d/packages" ] && [ -f "$d/build.sh" ]; then
      printf '%s' "$d"
      return 0
    fi
    d=$(dirname "$d")
  done
  return 1
}

root_dir=$(find_root "$script_dir") || {
  printf 'cannot locate the openvela root above %s\n' "$script_dir" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Where the feature sources live. apps/packages symlinks to packages/, so a
# build always compiles packages/ai_agent; a dev worktree is staged in and taken
# back out. Prefer an explicit override, then a worktree, then the package.
pkg_dir="${REMOTE_CTRL_PKG_DIR:-}"
if [ -z "$pkg_dir" ]; then
  if [ -d "$root_dir/.worktrees/ai-agent-remote-ctrl/src/remote" ]; then
    pkg_dir="$root_dir/.worktrees/ai-agent-remote-ctrl"
  else
    pkg_dir="$root_dir/packages/ai_agent"
  fi
fi

input.new_string:
# deskmate-demo.sh:96 hardcodes this window name for the `mimo attach` TUI.
MIMO_WINDOW="deskmate-mimo"

mimo_window_exists() {
  tmux list-windows -t "$TMUX_SESSION" -F '#{window_name}' 2>/dev/null |
    grep -qxF "$MIMO_WINDOW"
}

device_pane_count() {
  tmux list-panes -t "$TMUX_SESSION:device" 2>/dev/null | wc -l
}

# The DeskMate flow had the agent's own screen and the device console visible at
# the same time. Reproduce that: device console left, mimo TUI right, in one
# window. Idempotent — a second call finds the panes already joined.
split_device_and_mimo() {
  if [ "$(device_pane_count)" -ge 2 ]; then
    return 0
  fi
  mimo_window_exists || return 1
  tmux join-pane -h -l 50% -s "$TMUX_SESSION:$MIMO_WINDOW" -t "$TMUX_SESSION:device" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  # Keep the keyboard on the device console; the TUI is there to be watched.
  tmux select-pane -t "$TMUX_SESSION:device.0" 2>/dev/null || true
  return 0
}

do_attach() {
  tmux has-session -t "$TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null || die "nothing running; '$(basename "$0") up' first"

  if split_device_and_mimo; then
    say "device console on the left, mimo TUI on the right"
    say "switch panes with Ctrl-b then o (or Ctrl-b then arrow); detach with Ctrl-b then d"
  else
    warn "no $MIMO_WINDOW window to pair with (backend=$BACKEND, or mimo attach is off)"
    warn "attaching the device console alone"
  fi
  sleep 1
  exec tmux attach -t "$TMUX_SESSION" \; select-window -t device
}

do_mimo() {
  tmux has-session -t "$TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null || die "nothing running; '$(basename "$0") up' first"
  # If a previous `attach` folded it into the device window, pull it back out so
  # the TUI gets the full terminal.
  if ! mimo_window_exists && [ "$(device_pane_count)" -ge 2 ]; then
    tmux break-pane -d -s "$TMUX_SESSION:device.1" -n "$MIMO_WINDOW" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  mimo_window_exists || die "no mimo TUI running; it needs backend=mimo with attach enabled"
  say "mimo TUI full screen; detach with Ctrl-b then d"
  sleep 1
  exec tmux attach -t "$TMUX_SESSION" \; select-window -t "$MIMO_WINDOW"
}

脚本挪好了,但实测撞出一个**我 feature 代码里的真缺陷**,比脚本的事更要紧,先说这个。

## 你按方向键之后发生了什么

日志里有成串 `^[[A`/`^[[B`——agent CLI 不支持方向键翻历史,回了 `Unknown command`。之后 agent 退出(无 assert、无 panic,是干净退出),提示符落回 `goldfish-armv8a-ap>`,所以 `remote_status` 成了 `command not found`。这部分只是体验问题。

真问题在重启之后。我重发 `ai_agent`、**故意不重发** `set_remote`,它自己打出了 `initialized (broker=10.189.140.244:1883 device=goldfish-1)`——配置落盘是好的。但紧接着:

```
[remote_ctrl] started
[remote] a transport loop is still active, not starting another
```

然后 `remote_status` 永远是 `State: Offline / Chat turns: no`。MQTT 上 bridge 还在往 `bridge-to-device` 发 snapshot,而 `device-to-bridge` 十秒内一条都没有。

## 根因

`CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT=y`(我在实际 `.config` 里确认过),整个系统一个地址空间,`ai_agent` 退出**不会**重置 static 变量。我那个所有权守卫是这么写的:

- `remote_link_mqtt.c:79` `static bool g_loop_active`
- `:286` 起新循环前发现它为 true 就拒绝
- `:386` 只在循环正常走完才 `release_loop()`

Ctrl-C 退出绕过了 `agent_main.c:741` 的 teardown,传输线程被连带杀掉、走不到 `release_loop()`,`g_loop_active` 就永久卡在 true。此后每次 `ai_agent` 都被拒,**只能重启模拟器才能恢复**。

讽刺的是这个守卫本身是我为了修「重启竞态」加的,它挡住了两个循环并存,却没考虑持有者非正常死亡——典型的只处理了正常路径。

顺带说一句,我本来想用 `kill(pid, 0)` 探活来判断旧持有者是否还在,查了 `nuttx/include/signal.h:306` 发现 `GOOD_SIGNO(0)` 在这里是**真**(`0 <= 63`),也就是 signo 0 会被真派发而不是仅做存在性检查,和 POSIX 语义不同。这条路不通,得靠记录 owner pid 之类的办法。

## 你现在的处境

设备上那个 agent 已经进了这个状态,`down` 再 `up` 才能恢复。**规避办法:退出 agent 用 `quit`,不要用 Ctrl-C**——`quit` 走 `cmd_channel.c:191`/`212` 的正常 teardown,会释放守卫。

## 脚本那边(已完成)

- 已放到 `contest2026_272_tokenwujixian/tools/acp-bridge/bin/remote-ctrl-demo.sh`,和 `deskmate-demo.sh` 并列,worktree 里那份已删,只剩一份
- 路径不再按层数硬算,改成向上找 `nuttx/` + `packages/` + `build.sh` 三个标记,所以放哪都能用;`BRIDGE_DIR` 也从自身位置推导,不再写死团队仓库名
- `attach` 现在是**一屏两栏**:左设备控制台、右 mimo TUI,焦点默认在左边;新增 `mimo` 子命令单独全屏看 TUI。实测 `join-pane -l 50%` 在你的 tmux 3.2a 上可用、幂等、`break` 能还原
- 所有 `send-keys` 改成按 pane id 解析(靠 `pane_start_command` 里的 `emulator.sh` 认人),不再写 `device.0`——否则别人配了 `pane-base-index 1`,`verify` 会把权限决策敲进 mimo 的对话框

要我现在就修那个所有权守卫吗?思路是给守卫记上 owner pid,新实例发现持有者不是自己就判定为陈旧并接管,同时给 `remote_ctrl_channel_init` 加一条陈旧回收。改完要重编 + 重跑 fake 后端那套断言。

# ── The device is yours ───────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# This script deliberately stops at the PC boundary, exactly as
# deskmate-demo.sh does: it owns the broker check, the bridge and the mimo
# attach window, and nothing else. Booting the emulator and typing at the
# device console are the operator's job — a script that drives the console
# through `tmux send-keys` also owns stdin, which is precisely what the device
# side must not surrender (the agent has to stay in the foreground), and it
# would fake the human half of a permission decision.
#
# What the script can do is tell you exactly what to type, with the addresses
# and credentials already substituted.
device_instructions() {
  cat <<EOF
On the device (its own terminal, not this one):

  ./emulator.sh $BUILD_DIR -no-window     # or however you boot it

At the NSH prompt ('$NSH_PROMPT'):

  ai_agent                                    # keep it in the FOREGROUND, no '&'

At the agent prompt ('$AGENT_PROMPT'):
EOF
  if [ -n "$MQTT_USERNAME" ]; then
    printf '\n  set_remote_auth %s %s\n' "$MQTT_USERNAME" "$MQTT_PASSWORD"
  fi
  cat <<EOF

  set_remote $HOST_ADDRESS:$BROKER_PORT $DEVICE_ID

Both are persisted, so after the first time only 'ai_agent' is needed. Leave
the agent with 'quit' rather than Ctrl-C: Ctrl-C skips its teardown and the
transport keeps the link claimed until the device reboots.

Then, at the agent prompt:

  remote_status                  link state, billing, whether approval is pending
  remote_ask <instruction>       send one instruction to the remote agent
  remote_output                  the remote agent's reply so far
  remote_once / remote_deny      answer a permission request (human only)
EOF
}

# Verification from the PC is observation, not puppetry: it watches the live MQTT
# link and reports what the device is actually doing. It never types at the
# device console — that console is yours, and a decision typed by a script would
# not be a human approval.
VERIFY_WINDOW_S="${REMOTE_CTRL_VERIFY_WINDOW_S:-14}"

do_verify() {
  command -v mosquitto_sub > /dev/null || die "mosquitto_sub not installed"
  pgrep -f "[d]eskmate-bridge.mjs" > /dev/null ||
    die "the bridge is not running; '$(basename "$0") up' first"

  local traffic dev2br br2dev
  say "watching $TOPIC_PREFIX/$DEVICE_ID/# for ${VERIFY_WINDOW_S}s"
  # -W ends the subscription; it exits non-zero on that timeout, which is the
  # normal path here.
  traffic=$(timeout $((VERIFY_WINDOW_S + 6)) mosquitto_sub \
    -h "$HOST_ADDRESS" -p "$BROKER_PORT" \
    ${MQTT_USERNAME:+-u "$MQTT_USERNAME"} ${MQTT_PASSWORD:+-P "$MQTT_PASSWORD"} \
    -t "$TOPIC_PREFIX/$DEVICE_ID/#" -v -W "$VERIFY_WINDOW_S" 2>/dev/null || true)

  dev2br=$(grep -cF 'device-to-bridge' <<< "$traffic" || true)
  br2dev=$(grep -cF 'bridge-to-device' <<< "$traffic" || true)

  printf '\n'
  say "bridge -> device : $br2dev message(s)"
  say "device -> bridge : $dev2br message(s)"
  printf '\n'

  if [ "$br2dev" -eq 0 ] && [ "$dev2br" -eq 0 ]; then
    die "silent link: the bridge is running but nothing is on the wire"
  fi

  if [ "$dev2br" -eq 0 ]; then
    warn "the bridge is publishing but the device is not answering"
    warn "so the PC half is fine and the device is not linked yet"
    printf '\n'
    device_instructions
    return 1
  fi

  # Distinct types prove distinct properties, so report them individually
  # instead of collapsing everything into one pass/fail.
  local t
  for t in hello prompt_submit decision usage_query; do
    grep -F 'device-to-bridge' <<< "$traffic" | grep -qF "\"type\":\"$t\"" &&
      say "  device sent $t"
  done
  for t in hello_ack snapshot usage_snapshot; do
    grep -F 'bridge-to-device' <<< "$traffic" | grep -qF "\"type\":\"$t\"" &&
      say "  bridge sent $t"
  done

  printf '\n'
  say "the device is linked and both directions are live"
  cat <<EOF

What this proves from here: the device reached the broker, the bridge answered,
and traffic flows both ways. What it cannot prove from here is anything that
needs a human at the device console — a prompt you type, or an approval you
give. For those, watch them land: run '$(basename "$0") wire' in one terminal
and type at the device in another.
EOF
}

do_status() {
  printf 'bridge   : %s\n' "$(pgrep -f "[d]eskmate-bridge.mjs" > /dev/null && echo up || echo down)"
  # No device line here on purpose. The device may be another machine or a real

  printf 'device   : ask the wire — %s verify\n' "$(basename "$0")"

text: `device` 和 `status` 都对了。但 `verify` 有个路径我得先修:没接设备时线上会完全安静,现在只会 `die "silent link"` 就走,而最可能的原因恰恰是「设备还没启」——该顺手把要敲的命令打出来。

    die "silent link: the bridge is running but nothing is on the wire"

input.new_string:
# Total silence is the expected state before a device shows up: the bridge only
  # starts publishing once a hello has arrived. So say what is missing and how to
  # supply it rather than just failing.
  if [ "$br2dev" -eq 0 ] && [ "$dev2br" -eq 0 ]; then
    warn "nothing on the wire at all — the PC half is up but no device has spoken"
    printf '\n'
    device_instructions
    printf '\n'
    warn "then run '$(basename "$0") verify' again"
    return 1
  fi

## 分工

PC 侧(脚本管):broker 探测、bridge、mimo attach 窗口、镜像编译与断言、attach 端口避让。
设备侧(你管):启模拟器、`ai_agent`、`set_remote_auth`、`set_remote`、所有 `remote_*` 命令。

`send-keys` 一个都不剩(只剩一行注释说明为什么不能有),`down` 也不再杀模拟器——那是你的设备,脚本没启过它,就不该动它。

## 改动要点

`device` 子命令现在把你要敲的命令原样打出来,地址和凭据已代入:


`verify` 从「替你敲命令」改成「看线上流量」——订阅 `deskmate/goldfish-1/#` 一段时间,分别数两个方向的报文,并按类型报告(`hello` / `prompt_submit` / `decision` / `hello_ack` / `snapshot` / `usage_snapshot`)。设备没接时它不再只是报错,而是把该敲的命令打出来,返回 1。实测过这条路径。

`attach` 改成 bridge 日志 + mimo TUI 并排,键盘默认给 TUI;`mimo` 单独全屏。

我原本把分屏配到 `bridge` 窗口,实测发现那是个**空启动器**——`deskmate-demo.sh:171` 在开了 `--mimo-attach` 时会把真 bridge 挪进自己的 `deskmate-bridge` 窗口,启动器里只剩死 shell。所以带 `deskmate>` 提示符的是另一个窗口。改成动态解析后验过:`bridge_window()` → `deskmate-bridge`,pane `%2` 跑的是 `node`,左侧确实是 `deskmate>` 提示符。这个测试是加载脚本真函数跑的,不是复刻。

# Distinct types prove distinct properties, so report them individually
  # instead of collapsing everything into one pass/fail.
  #
  # Each direction is split out once and matched from that cache. Chaining
  # `grep dir | grep -q type` would let the reader exit on its first hit and
  # SIGPIPE the writer; `set -o pipefail` then reports 141 and the type is
  # silently dropped from the report even though it was on the wire. Measured
  # at 141 on a large capture, so this is the busy-link case, not a corner one.
  local t outbound inbound
  outbound=$(grep -F 'device-to-bridge' <<< "$traffic" || true)
  inbound=$(grep -F 'bridge-to-device' <<< "$traffic" || true)

  for t in hello prompt_submit decision usage_query; do
    if grep -qF "\"type\":\"$t\"" <<< "$outbound"; then
      say "  device sent $t"
    fi
  done
  for t in hello_ack snapshot usage_snapshot; do
    if grep -qF "\"type\":\"$t\"" <<< "$inbound"; then

input.old_string: mimo_window_exists() { window_exists "$MIMO_WINDOW"; }
input.new_string:
mimo_window_exists() { window_exists "$MIMO_WINDOW"; }

# A grouped tmux session, so the GUI window below and a later `attach` can show
# different windows instead of fighting over one shared "current window".
VIEW_SESSION="${TMUX_SESSION}-view"

view_session_exists() { tmux has-session -t "$VIEW_SESSION" 2>/dev/null; }

gui_terminal() {
  [ "${REMOTE_CTRL_GUI:-1}" = 1 ] || return 1
  [ -n "${DISPLAY:-}" ] || [ -n "${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-}" ] || return 1
  local t
  for t in gnome-terminal x-terminal-emulator xterm konsole; do
    command -v "$t" > /dev/null && { printf '%s' "$t"; return 0; }
  done
  return 1
}

# Run outside tmux, deskmate-demo.sh pops a GNOME Terminal for `mimo attach`
# (deskmate-demo.sh:99). We run it inside tmux, so it takes its other branch and
# parks the TUI in a tmux window instead — which nobody sees until someone
# attaches. Open one GUI window on that pane to restore the original feel.
open_gui_view() {
  local term cmd
  term=$(gui_terminal) || return 1
  mimo_window_exists || return 1

  view_session_exists ||
    tmux new-session -d -s "$VIEW_SESSION" -t "$TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null ||
    return 1

  # Point the grouped session at the TUI before attaching, rather than passing
  # tmux a `\;`-separated command list through another shell's quoting.
  tmux select-window -t "$VIEW_SESSION:$MIMO_WINDOW" 2>/dev/null || true

  cmd="tmux attach -t $VIEW_SESSION"
  case "$term" in
    gnome-terminal)
      setsid "$term" --title="remote-ctrl: mimo" -- bash -lc "$cmd" > /dev/null 2>&1 & ;;
    konsole)
      setsid "$term" -e bash -lc "$cmd" > /dev/null 2>&1 & ;;
    *)
      setsid "$term" -e bash -lc "$cmd" > /dev/null 2>&1 & ;;
  esac
  disown 2>/dev/null || true
  return 0
}

## 之前为什么没有窗口

根因在 `deskmate-demo.sh:91-107` 的 `open_mimo_attach()`,它分两条路:**在 tmux 里**就 `new-window`,**不在 tmux 里**才弹 GNOME Terminal。你原来直接跑 deskmate 时不在 tmux 中,窗口自己就弹了;我的脚本把 bridge 塞进 tmux,于是走了第一条路,TUI 进了一个 detached 会话里的窗口——进程一直活着,只是没人附着,所以你看不见。

view_session_exists() { tmux has-session -t "$VIEW_SESSION" 2>/dev/null; }

# Closing the GUI window leaves the session behind with no client — measured. So
# "a window is showing the TUI" is a question about attached clients, not about
# the session existing, or `attach` would keep refusing to pair panes long after

view_session_live() {
  local n
  view_session_exists || return 1
  n=$(tmux display-message -p -t "$VIEW_SESSION" '#{session_attached}' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  [ "${n:-0}" -gt 0 ]

# Run outside tmux, deskmate-demo.sh pops a GNOME Terminal for `mimo attach`
# (deskmate-demo.sh:99). We run it inside tmux, so it takes its other branch and

input.new_string:
# start_bridge returns as soon as the bridge process exists, but deskmate-demo.sh
# only creates the mimo window later: it first waits up to 30s for its ACP ready
# file (deskmate-demo.sh:173) and opens the window at :184. Measured: without this
# wait the window is not there yet, open_gui_view silently does nothing, and no
# window ever appears. Waits slightly past that 30s deadline.
wait_for_mimo_window() {
  # Nothing to wait for when no attach was requested — don't stall for 35s.
  { [ "$MIMO_ATTACH" = 1 ] && [ "$BACKEND" = "mimo" ]; } || return 1

  local i
  for i in $(seq 1 35); do
    mimo_window_exists && return 0
    sleep 1
  done
  warn "the mimo attach window never appeared within 35s"
  return 1
}

## 这轮修了三处

**`down` 会漏掉 mimo TUI**。分组 tmux 会话有个陷阱:kill 组里一个会话,另一个会存活,面板里的进程也继续跑(我用一次性会话实测确认)。原来只 kill 主会话,GUI 窗口和 TUI 会残留。现在先 kill view 会话。

**你这次 `up` 没弹窗,是个真 bug**。根因是时序:`start_bridge` 只等 bridge 进程出现再 `sleep 3` 就返回,而 `deskmate-demo.sh` 要先等它的 ACP ready 文件(`:173`,最多 30 秒)才在 `:184` 建 mimo 窗口。所以 `open_gui_view` 跑得太早,`mimo_window_exists` 为假,两个分支都没进——连警告都没打,所以你只看到「什么都没发生」。加了等待(最多 35 秒,略超它那个 30 秒期限;没开 attach 时立刻返回,不白等)。

# A grouped tmux session, so the GUI window below and a later `attach` can show
# different windows instead of fighting over one shared "current window".
VIEW_SESSION="${TMUX_SESSION}-view"

view_session_exists() { tmux has-session -t "$VIEW_SESSION" 2>/dev/null; }

# Closing the GUI window leaves the session behind with no client — measured. So
# "a window is showing the TUI" is a question about attached clients, not about
# the session existing, or `attach` would keep refusing to pair panes long after
# the window is gone.
view_session_live() {
  local n
  view_session_exists || return 1
  n=$(tmux display-message -p -t "$VIEW_SESSION" '#{session_attached}' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  [ "${n:-0}" -gt 0 ]
}
input.new_string:
# Each GUI window gets its OWN grouped session. Sessions in a group share the
# window list but keep their own current window, so one window can sit on the
# bridge log while another sits on the mimo TUI. A single shared session would
# make the two windows fight over which window is current.
VIEW_PREFIX="${TMUX_SESSION}-view"

view_session_for() { printf '%s-%s' "$VIEW_PREFIX" "$1"; }

view_session_exists() { tmux has-session -t "$(view_session_for "$1")" 2>/dev/null; }

# Closing a GUI window leaves its session behind with no client — measured. So
# "a window is showing this" is a question about attached clients, not about the
# session existing, or `attach` would keep refusing to pair panes long after the
# window is gone.
view_session_live() {
  local s n
  s=$(view_session_for "$1")
  tmux has-session -t "$s" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  n=$(tmux display-message -p -t "$s" '#{session_attached}' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  [ "${n:-0}" -gt 0 ]
}

# Every view session this script created, for teardown.
view_sessions() {
  local names
  names=$(tmux list-sessions -F '#{session_name}' 2>/dev/null || true)
  grep -E "^${VIEW_PREFIX}-" <<< "$names" || true
}

input.new_string:
# open_gui_view <tmux-window> <window-title>
#
# Pops one GUI terminal showing that tmux window, so both halves of the PC side
# are presented the same way DeskMate presented them: a real window each, not one
# visible and one buried in a tmux session nobody attached.
open_gui_view() {
  local win="$1" title="$2" term session cmd
  term=$(gui_terminal) || return 1
  window_exists "$win" || return 1

  # Already got a window on it — don't stack a second one.
  view_session_live "$win" && return 0

  session=$(view_session_for "$win")
  tmux has-session -t "$session" 2>/dev/null ||
    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -t "$TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null ||
    return 1

  # Point this session at its window before attaching, rather than passing tmux a
  # `\;`-separated command list through another shell's quoting.
  tmux select-window -t "$session:$win" 2>/dev/null || true

  cmd="tmux attach -t $session"
  case "$term" in
    gnome-terminal)
      setsid "$term" --title="$title" -- bash -lc "$cmd" > /dev/null 2>&1 & ;;
    *)
      setsid "$term" -e bash -lc "$cmd" > /dev/null 2>&1 & ;;
  esac
  disown 2>/dev/null || true
  return 0
}

input.new_string:
# `attach` means "show me the views again" — after closing a window, or from a
# terminal that never had them. With a GUI it re-opens the same windows `up`
# opened, which is idempotent. Without one (ssh, no DISPLAY) it falls back to
# taking over this terminal, and only then does pane splitting make sense.
do_attach() {
  tmux has-session -t "$TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null || die "nothing running; '$(basename "$0") up' first"

  if open_gui_views; then
    say "windows open: bridge log, and the mimo agent"
    say "the device console is not among them — that one is yours, on the device"
    return 0
  fi

  warn "no GUI terminal, so this terminal becomes the view"
  # 2 is "declined on purpose", distinct from 1 "nothing to pair with" — the two
  # deserve different explanations rather than one catch-all warning.
  local rc=0
  split_bridge_and_mimo || rc=$?
  case "$rc" in
    0)
      say "bridge log on the left, mimo TUI on the right (keyboard is on the TUI)"
      say "switch panes with Ctrl-b then o; detach with Ctrl-b then d" ;;
    2)
      say "the mimo TUI already has a window of its own, leaving it there" ;;
    *)
      warn "no $MIMO_WINDOW window to pair with (backend=$BACKEND, or mimo attach is off)" ;;
  esac
  sleep 1
  exec tmux attach -t "$TMUX_SESSION" \; select-window -t "$(bridge_window)"
}

do_mimo() {
  tmux has-session -t "$TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null || die "nothing running; '$(basename "$0") up' first"
  # If a no-GUI `attach` folded it into the bridge window, pull it back out so the
  # TUI gets a whole terminal again.
  local tui
  if ! mimo_window_exists && [ "$(bridge_pane_count)" -ge 2 ]; then
    tui=$(mimo_pane_in_bridge_window) &&
      tmux break-pane -d -s "$tui" -n "$MIMO_WINDOW" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  mimo_window_exists || die "no mimo TUI running; it needs backend=mimo with attach enabled"

  if open_gui_view "$MIMO_WINDOW" "remote-ctrl: mimo agent"; then
    say "the mimo agent window is open"
    return 0
  fi

  warn "no GUI terminal, so this terminal becomes the view"
  say "detach with Ctrl-b then d"
  sleep 1
  exec tmux attach -t "$TMUX_SESSION" \; select-window -t "$MIMO_WINDOW"
}

## 期间抓到一个真 bug

第一次跑完两窗口版本时,**两个窗口都显示 mimo TUI**,bridge 那个是错的。根因:`deskmate-demo.sh:96` 建 mimo 窗口时**没带 `-d`**,tmux 会选中新窗口;而这两个 view 会话是分组的、共享窗口列表,于是我先前已经钉在 `deskmate-bridge` 的那个会话被拖着一起跳过去了。修法是等所有窗口就位后再重新钉一次(`pin_view_windows`)。修完在实况上验过:修复前两个都指向 `deskmate-mimo`,修复后各自归位;完整 `up` 重跑一遍也成立。

`attach` 的语义变了——它现在是「把窗口叫回来」,关掉窗口后用它恢复,幂等(实测调用前后客户端数都是 2,没叠新窗口)。没有图形环境时(ssh、无 DISPLAY)才退回原来接管终端的行为,那时才做左右分屏。

关窗仍然**不等于退出**,`down` 是唯一的正常退出。

`up` 的输出里我写了窗口标题 `remote-ctrl: bridge` / `remote-ctrl: mimo agent`,用的是 `gnome-terminal --title=`。但 tmux 自己也会设终端标题,很可能把它覆盖掉——**标题实际显示成什么我没验证**。如果你看到的窗口标题不是这两个名字,那是我这句提示不准,不影响功能。要我改成用 tmux 的 `set-titles` 来确保标题正确吗?

  # ── Tree preparation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  
  # apps/packages is a symlink to packages/, so any build compiles
  # packages/ai_agent and never a worktree. Feature code is therefore staged in,
  # and taken back out by `down`.
  stage_sources() {
    local target="$root_dir/packages/ai_agent"
  
    if [ "$pkg_dir" = "$target" ]; then
      say "sources already live in packages/ai_agent, nothing to stage"
      mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"; : > "$COPIED_LIST"
      return 0
    fi
  
    git -C "$pkg_dir" rev-parse --git-dir > /dev/null 2>&1 ||
      die "$pkg_dir is not a git repo, so the file set cannot be determined"
  
    local base
    base=$(git -C "$pkg_dir" rev-parse --abbrev-ref '@{upstream}' 2>/dev/null || echo "work/next")
  
    local files
    files=$( { git -C "$pkg_dir" diff --name-only "$base";
               git -C "$pkg_dir" ls-files --others --exclude-standard; } | sort -u )
    [ -n "$files" ] || die "no changes found in $pkg_dir versus $base"
  
    # Never clobber someone else's uncommitted work in the shared package.
    if [ ! -f "$COPIED_LIST" ] && [ "$(git -C "$target" status --porcelain | wc -l)" -ne 0 ]; then
      git -C "$target" status --porcelain >&2
      die "packages/ai_agent has uncommitted changes; commit or stash them first"
    fi
  
    say "staging $(printf '%s\n' "$files" | wc -l) files into packages/ai_agent"
    mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"; : > "$COPIED_LIST"
    local f
    while IFS= read -r f; do
      [ -n "$f" ] || continue
      mkdir -p "$target/$(dirname "$f")"
      cp -p "$pkg_dir/$f" "$target/$f"
      cmp -s "$pkg_dir/$f" "$target/$f" || die "copy mismatch for $f"
      printf '%s\n' "$f" >> "$COPIED_LIST"
    done <<< "$files"
  }
  
  unstage_sources() {
    local target="$root_dir/packages/ai_agent"
  
    [ -f "$COPIED_LIST" ] || return 0
    if [ "$pkg_dir" = "$target" ]; then rm -f "$COPIED_LIST"; return 0; fi
  
    say "removing staged files from packages/ai_agent"
    local f tracked=()
    while IFS= read -r f; do
      [ -n "$f" ] || continue
      if git -C "$target" ls-files --error-unmatch "$f" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        tracked+=("$f")
      else
        rm -f "$target/$f"
      fi
    done < "$COPIED_LIST"
  
    [ ${#tracked[@]} -gt 0 ] && git -C "$target" checkout -- "${tracked[@]}"
    rmdir "$target/src/remote" "$target/tests/host" "$target/tests" 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -f "$COPIED_LIST"
  }
  
  # The board defconfig is shared and routinely carries uncommitted local edits,
  # so it is restored from an exact byte copy. `git checkout` would silently throw
  # those edits away.
  enable_config() {
    if grep -q '^CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REMOTE_CTRL=y' "$DEFCONFIG"; then
      say "CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REMOTE_CTRL already enabled"
      return 0
    fi
  
    mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
    [ -f "$DEFCONFIG_BACKUP" ] || cp -p "$DEFCONFIG" "$DEFCONFIG_BACKUP"
    say "enabling CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REMOTE_CTRL (backup at $DEFCONFIG_BACKUP)"
    # defconfig is savedefconfig output, so keep it sorted.
    awk '
      !inserted && /^CONFIG_A/ && $0 > "CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REMOTE_CTRL=y" {
        print "CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REMOTE_CTRL=y"; inserted = 1
      }
      { print }
      END { if (!inserted) print "CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REMOTE_CTRL=y" }
    ' "$DEFCONFIG" > "$DEFCONFIG.tmp"
    mv "$DEFCONFIG.tmp" "$DEFCONFIG"
    grep -q '^CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REMOTE_CTRL=y' "$DEFCONFIG" || die "config insert failed"
  }
  
  restore_config() {
    [ -f "$DEFCONFIG_BACKUP" ] || return 0
    say "restoring the board defconfig from its backup"
    cp -p "$DEFCONFIG_BACKUP" "$DEFCONFIG"
    cmp -s "$DEFCONFIG_BACKUP" "$DEFCONFIG" || die "defconfig restore is not byte-identical"
    rm -f "$DEFCONFIG_BACKUP"

    grep -q '^CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REMOTE_CTRL=y' "$out/.config" ||

      \( -name 'remote_*.c.o' -o -name 'tool_remote_agent.c.o' \) 2>/dev/null | wc -l)

    local strings_file="$STATE_DIR/image-strings.txt"

    for marker in 'remote_agent_prompt' 'remote_agent_status' 'set_remote_auth' \
                  'device-to-bridge' 'Prompt sent. Use remote_status'; do
      grep -qF "$marker" "$strings_file" || {
        rm -f "$strings_file"
        die "marker missing from image: $marker"
      }
    done
    rm -f "$strings_file"
  
    say "image verified: config on, 6 objects, all markers present"
  }
  
  do_build() {
    command -v cmake > /dev/null || die "cmake not found"
    stage_sources
    enable_config
    say "building $BOARD_CONFIG into $BUILD_DIR (a few minutes)"
    ( cd "$root_dir" && ./build.sh "$BOARD_CONFIG/" --cmake -b "$BUILD_DIR" -j"$(nproc)" )
    assert_image
    say "build done. Next: $(basename "$0") up"
  }
  
  # ── Services ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  
  broker_reachable() {
    timeout 5 mosquitto_pub -h "$HOST_ADDRESS" -p "$BROKER_PORT" \
      ${MQTT_USERNAME:+-u "$MQTT_USERNAME"} ${MQTT_PASSWORD:+-P "$MQTT_PASSWORD"} \
      -t "$TOPIC_PREFIX/_probe" -m probe > /dev/null 2>&1
  }
  
  check_broker() {
    command -v mosquitto_pub > /dev/null || { warn "mosquitto_pub absent, skipping the broker probe"; return 0; }
    if broker_reachable; then
      say "broker reachable at $HOST_ADDRESS:$BROKER_PORT"
      return 0
    fi
    warn "cannot publish to $HOST_ADDRESS:$BROKER_PORT with the supplied credentials"
    warn "export DESKMATE_MQTT_USERNAME / DESKMATE_MQTT_PASSWORD, or run '$(basename "$0") broker'"
    die "broker check failed"
  }
  
  # Only for machines with no broker of their own. Loopback-bound and anonymous,
  # so nothing on the LAN can reach it; the device must then dial 10.0.2.2.
  start_broker() {
    command -v mosquitto > /dev/null || die "mosquitto not installed"
    mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
    cat > "$BROKER_CONF" <<EOF
  # Local fallback broker for the remote-ctrl demo. Loopback only and anonymous:
  # the emulator reaches it through its NAT gateway (10.0.2.2) while nothing on
  # the LAN can use it.
  listener ${REMOTE_CTRL_LOCAL_BROKER_PORT:-1884} 127.0.0.1
  allow_anonymous true
  EOF
    say "starting a local broker on 127.0.0.1:${REMOTE_CTRL_LOCAL_BROKER_PORT:-1884}"
    setsid nohup mosquitto -c "$BROKER_CONF" > "$BROKER_LOG" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
    disown || true
    sleep 2
    local listeners
    listeners=$(ss -ltn 2>/dev/null || true)
    grep -q ":${REMOTE_CTRL_LOCAL_BROKER_PORT:-1884} " <<< "$listeners" || {
      cat "$BROKER_LOG" >&2; die "local broker did not start"
    }
    cat <<EOF
  
  Point the demo at it with:
    export REMOTE_CTRL_HOST_ADDRESS=10.0.2.2
    export REMOTE_CTRL_BROKER_PORT=${REMOTE_CTRL_LOCAL_BROKER_PORT:-1884}
    unset DESKMATE_MQTT_USERNAME DESKMATE_MQTT_PASSWORD
  EOF
  }
  
  # `mimo acp --port N` binds that port rather than dialing an existing instance,
  # so the attach port cannot be shared: on any machine already running a mimo,
  # 4096 is usually held by it. Prefer the documented port, step past it when taken.
  port_free() {
    local listeners
    listeners=$(ss -ltn 2>/dev/null || true)
    ! grep -qE "[:.]$1[[:space:]]" <<< "$listeners"
  }
  
  pick_attach_port() {
    local p="$MIMO_ATTACH_PORT" limit=$((MIMO_ATTACH_PORT + 20))
    while [ "$p" -lt "$limit" ]; do
      port_free "$p" && { printf '%s' "$p"; return 0; }
      p=$((p + 1))
    done
    die "no free attach port between $MIMO_ATTACH_PORT and $limit"
  }
  
  # The PC half, including the mimo-attach handshake, is deskmate-demo.sh's job.
  start_bridge() {
    [ -x "$DEMO_SH" ] || die "not found or not executable: $DEMO_SH"
    [ -d "$BRIDGE_DIR/node_modules" ] || die "run 'npm install' in $BRIDGE_DIR first"
  
    # A second bridge on the same topic prefix would also answer the device's
    # hello, leaving two authorities racing over one session.
    pgrep -f "[d]eskmate-bridge.mjs" > /dev/null &&
      die "a bridge is already running; '$(basename "$0") down' first"
    if [ "$BACKEND" = "mimo" ]; then
      command -v "${DESKMATE_MIMO_BIN:-mimo}" > /dev/null ||
        die "the mimo backend needs '${DESKMATE_MIMO_BIN:-mimo}' on PATH"
    fi
  
    # The bridge reads credentials only from DESKMATE_MQTT_USERNAME/PASSWORD in its
    # environment, and a tmux window inherits the tmux *server's* environment
    # rather than this shell's. Hand them over through a 0600 file that the window
    # sources: putting them in the command line would expose the password in the
    # process list, and `tmux set-environment` would leave it readable via
    # `tmux show-environment`.
    local cmd=""
    if [ -n "$MQTT_USERNAME" ] || [ -n "$MQTT_PASSWORD" ]; then
      mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
      ( umask 077; cat > "$CRED_FILE" <<EOF
  export DESKMATE_MQTT_USERNAME=$(printf '%q' "$MQTT_USERNAME")
  export DESKMATE_MQTT_PASSWORD=$(printf '%q' "$MQTT_PASSWORD")
  EOF
      )
      cmd+=". $CRED_FILE && "
    fi
  
    cmd+="cd $BRIDGE_DIR && bin/deskmate-demo.sh bridge $BACKEND mqtt"
    cmd+=" --broker mqtt://$HOST_ADDRESS:$BROKER_PORT"
    cmd+=" --topic-prefix $TOPIC_PREFIX --device-id $DEVICE_ID"
    if [ "$MIMO_ATTACH" = 1 ] && [ "$BACKEND" = "mimo" ]; then
      local attach_port
      attach_port=$(pick_attach_port)
      if [ "$attach_port" != "$MIMO_ATTACH_PORT" ]; then
        warn "attach port $MIMO_ATTACH_PORT is in use (often by the mimo you are"
        warn "already running); using $attach_port instead"
      fi
      cmd+=" --mimo-attach --mimo-attach-port $attach_port"
    fi
  
    say "starting the bridge (backend=$BACKEND) via deskmate-demo.sh"
    # Run it inside tmux so its own --mimo-attach path can open a window for the
    # attach session.
    tmux new-window -t "$TMUX_SESSION" -n bridge "$cmd; exec ${SHELL:-/bin/bash}"
  
    local i
    for i in $(seq 1 40); do
      pgrep -f "[d]eskmate-bridge.mjs" > /dev/null && { say "bridge is up"; sleep 3; return 0; }
      sleep 1
    done
    # Deliberately the launcher window, not bridge_window(): on this path the
    # bridge never came up, so its own window may not exist and the launcher is
    # where deskmate-demo.sh printed why.
    tmux capture-pane -t "$TMUX_SESSION:bridge" -p | tail -20 >&2
    die "the bridge did not start"
  }
  
  # ── The device is yours ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  #
  # This script deliberately stops at the PC boundary, exactly as
  # deskmate-demo.sh does: it owns the broker check, the bridge and the mimo
  # attach window, and nothing else. Booting the emulator and typing at the
  # device console are the operator's job — a script that drives the console
  # through `tmux send-keys` also owns stdin, which is precisely what the device
  # side must not surrender (the agent has to stay in the foreground), and it
  # would fake the human half of a permission decision.
  #
  # What the script can do is tell you exactly what to type, with the addresses
  # and credentials already substituted.
  device_instructions() {
    cat <<EOF
  On the device (its own terminal, not this one):
  
    ./emulator.sh $BUILD_DIR -no-window     # or however you boot it
  
  At the NSH prompt ('$NSH_PROMPT'):
  
    ai_agent                                    # keep it in the FOREGROUND, no '&'
  
  At the agent prompt ('$AGENT_PROMPT'):
  EOF
    if [ -n "$MQTT_USERNAME" ]; then
      printf '\n  set_remote_auth %s %s\n' "$MQTT_USERNAME" "$MQTT_PASSWORD"
    fi
    cat <<EOF
  
    set_remote $HOST_ADDRESS:$BROKER_PORT $DEVICE_ID
  
  Both are persisted, so after the first time only 'ai_agent' is needed. Leave
  the agent with 'quit' rather than Ctrl-C: Ctrl-C skips its teardown and the
  transport keeps the link claimed until the device reboots.
  
  The remote_* commands are listed by 'help' on the device — not repeated here,
  since a copy in this script would be one more place to fall out of date.
  EOF
  }
  
  ensure_session() {
    tmux has-session -t "$TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null && return 0
    tmux new-session -d -s "$TMUX_SESSION" -x 220 -y 50 -n shell
  }
  
  do_up() {
    command -v tmux > /dev/null || die "tmux not installed"
    ensure_session
    check_broker
    start_bridge
  
    local gui_opened=0
    if open_gui_views; then
      gui_opened=1
    else
      warn "no GUI terminal available, so both views stay inside tmux"
      warn "see them with '$(basename "$0") attach'"
    fi
  
    cat <<EOF
  
  $(say "the PC side is up: broker reachable, bridge running, mimo attached")
  EOF
  
    # What to suggest depends on whether a window already popped up: with one open,
    # `attach` deliberately leaves the panes alone, so pointing at it as "put them
    # side by side" would promise something it will not do.
    if [ "$gui_opened" = 1 ]; then
      cat <<EOF
  
    Two windows just opened, the same two DeskMate gave you:
      'remote-ctrl: mimo agent'   the agent — type your instructions here
      'remote-ctrl: bridge'       the bridge log, with its 'deskmate>' prompt
  
    Closing a window does NOT stop anything; '$(basename "$0") attach' brings them back.
  
    reopen   : $(basename "$0") attach          re-open both windows
    traffic  : $(basename "$0") wire            live MQTT between device and bridge
    check    : $(basename "$0") verify          assert the device actually linked
    teardown : $(basename "$0") down            the only real exit
  EOF
    else
      cat <<EOF
  
    view     : $(basename "$0") attach          bridge log + mimo TUI, one screen
    agent    : $(basename "$0") mimo            mimo TUI alone, full screen
    traffic  : $(basename "$0") wire            live MQTT between device and bridge
    check    : $(basename "$0") verify          assert the device actually linked
    teardown : $(basename "$0") down
  
    In tmux: Ctrl-b o switches panes, Ctrl-b d leaves without stopping anything.
  EOF
    fi
  
    cat <<EOF
  
  $(device_instructions)
  EOF
    if [ "$BACKEND" = "fake" ]; then
      cat <<EOF
  
  With the fake backend you drive the permission request yourself. It expires
  after 30 seconds, so do the two steps back to back:
  
    1. this side, in the bridge pane : prompt
    2. the device, at 'vela>'        : remote_once   -> "Permission decision accepted by ACP"
  EOF
    else
      cat <<EOF
  
  Note on approvals with the $BACKEND backend: its ACP side approves tool calls
  itself, so no permission request reaches the device — measured with
  'remote_ask run git status in this repo', which came back as
  'tooluse...: completed' with nothing to approve. To exercise the human approval
  path, run this side against the deterministic backend instead:
  
    REMOTE_CTRL_BACKEND=fake $(basename "$0") down
    REMOTE_CTRL_BACKEND=fake $(basename "$0") up
  EOF
    fi
  }
  
  # ── Verify ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  
  # Verification from the PC is observation, not puppetry: it watches the live MQTT
  # link and reports what the device is actually doing. It never types at the
  # device console — that console is yours, and a decision typed by a script would
  # not be a human approval.
  VERIFY_WINDOW_S="${REMOTE_CTRL_VERIFY_WINDOW_S:-14}"
  
  do_verify() {
    command -v mosquitto_sub > /dev/null || die "mosquitto_sub not installed"
    pgrep -f "[d]eskmate-bridge.mjs" > /dev/null ||
      die "the bridge is not running; '$(basename "$0") up' first"
  
    local traffic dev2br br2dev
    say "watching $TOPIC_PREFIX/$DEVICE_ID/# for ${VERIFY_WINDOW_S}s"
    # -W ends the subscription; it exits non-zero on that timeout, which is the
    # normal path here.
    traffic=$(timeout $((VERIFY_WINDOW_S + 6)) mosquitto_sub \
      -h "$HOST_ADDRESS" -p "$BROKER_PORT" \
      ${MQTT_USERNAME:+-u "$MQTT_USERNAME"} ${MQTT_PASSWORD:+-P "$MQTT_PASSWORD"} \
      -t "$TOPIC_PREFIX/$DEVICE_ID/#" -v -W "$VERIFY_WINDOW_S" 2>/dev/null || true)
  
    dev2br=$(grep -cF 'device-to-bridge' <<< "$traffic" || true)
    br2dev=$(grep -cF 'bridge-to-device' <<< "$traffic" || true)
  
    printf '\n'
    say "bridge -> device : $br2dev message(s)"
    say "device -> bridge : $dev2br message(s)"
    printf '\n'
  
    # Total silence is the expected state before a device shows up: the bridge only
    # starts publishing once a hello has arrived. So say what is missing and how to
    # supply it rather than just failing.
    # On the failure paths the instructions are part of the diagnosis, so they go
    # to stderr with the warnings. Splitting them across stdout and stderr would
    # scramble their order the moment either stream is redirected.
    if [ "$br2dev" -eq 0 ] && [ "$dev2br" -eq 0 ]; then
      warn "nothing on the wire at all — the PC half is up but no device has spoken"
      {
        printf '\n'
        device_instructions
        printf '\n'
      } >&2
      warn "then run '$(basename "$0") verify' again"
      return 1
    fi
  
    if [ "$dev2br" -eq 0 ]; then
      warn "the bridge is publishing but the device is not answering"
      warn "so the PC half is fine and the device is not linked yet"
      { printf '\n'; device_instructions; } >&2
      return 1
    fi
  
    # Distinct types prove distinct properties, so report them individually
    # instead of collapsing everything into one pass/fail.
    #
    # Each direction is split out once and matched from that cache. Chaining
    # `grep dir | grep -q type` would let the reader exit on its first hit and
    # SIGPIPE the writer; `set -o pipefail` then reports 141 and the type is
    # silently dropped from the report even though it was on the wire. Measured
    # at 141 on a large capture, so this is the busy-link case, not a corner one.
    local t outbound inbound
    outbound=$(grep -F 'device-to-bridge' <<< "$traffic" || true)
    inbound=$(grep -F 'bridge-to-device' <<< "$traffic" || true)
  
    for t in hello prompt_submit decision usage_query; do
      if grep -qF "\"type\":\"$t\"" <<< "$outbound"; then
        say "  device sent $t"
      fi
    done
    for t in hello_ack snapshot usage_snapshot; do
      if grep -qF "\"type\":\"$t\"" <<< "$inbound"; then
        say "  bridge sent $t"
      fi
    done
  
    printf '\n'
    say "the device is linked and both directions are live"
    cat <<EOF
  
  What this proves from here: the device reached the broker, the bridge answered,
  and traffic flows both ways. What it cannot prove from here is anything that
  needs a human at the device console — a prompt you type, or an approval you
  give. For those, watch them land: run '$(basename "$0") wire' in one terminal
  and type at the device in another.
  EOF
  }
  
  # ── Helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  
  do_status() {
    printf 'bridge   : %s\n' "$(pgrep -f "[d]eskmate-bridge.mjs" > /dev/null && echo up || echo down)"
    # No device line here on purpose. The device may be another machine or a real
    # board, so a local `pgrep qemu` would report "down" for a perfectly healthy
    # setup. Whether the device is linked is a question about the wire: `verify`.
    printf 'device   : ask the wire — %s verify\n' "$(basename "$0")"
    printf 'tmux     : %s\n' "$(tmux has-session -t "$TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null && echo "session $TMUX_SESSION" || echo none)"
    printf 'broker   : %s\n' "$HOST_ADDRESS:$BROKER_PORT${MQTT_USERNAME:+ (user $MQTT_USERNAME)}"
    if [ -f "$root_dir/$BUILD_DIR/nuttx" ]; then
      printf 'image    : %s (%s)\n' "$BUILD_DIR/nuttx" "$(date -r "$root_dir/$BUILD_DIR/nuttx" '+%F %T')"
    else
      printf 'image    : not built\n'
    fi
    [ -f "$COPIED_LIST" ] && printf 'staged   : %s files in packages/ai_agent\n' "$(wc -l < "$COPIED_LIST")"
    [ -f "$DEFCONFIG_BACKUP" ] && printf 'defconfig: modified, backup kept\n'
    return 0
  }
  
  do_wire() {
    command -v mosquitto_sub > /dev/null || die "mosquitto_sub not installed"
    say "following $TOPIC_PREFIX/# on $HOST_ADDRESS:$BROKER_PORT — Ctrl-C to stop"
    exec mosquitto_sub -h "$HOST_ADDRESS" -p "$BROKER_PORT" \
      ${MQTT_USERNAME:+-u "$MQTT_USERNAME"} ${MQTT_PASSWORD:+-P "$MQTT_PASSWORD"} \
      -t "$TOPIC_PREFIX/#" -v
  }
  
  # deskmate-demo.sh:96 hardcodes this window name for the `mimo attach` TUI.
  MIMO_WINDOW="deskmate-mimo"
  
  # Cached rather than piped straight into grep: under `set -o pipefail` grep can
  # exit first and SIGPIPE tmux, turning a found window into a reported failure.
  window_exists() {
    local wins
    wins=$(tmux list-windows -t "$TMUX_SESSION" -F '#{window_name}' 2>/dev/null || true)
    grep -qxF "$1" <<< "$wins"
  }
  
  mimo_window_exists() { window_exists "$MIMO_WINDOW"; }
  
  # Each GUI window gets its OWN grouped session. Sessions in a group share the
  # window list but keep their own current window, so one window can sit on the
  # bridge log while another sits on the mimo TUI. A single shared session would
  # make the two windows fight over which window is current.
  VIEW_PREFIX="${TMUX_SESSION}-view"
  
  view_session_for() { printf '%s-%s' "$VIEW_PREFIX" "$1"; }
  
  view_session_exists() { tmux has-session -t "$(view_session_for "$1")" 2>/dev/null; }
  
  # Closing a GUI window leaves its session behind with no client — measured. So
  # "a window is showing this" is a question about attached clients, not about the
  # session existing, or `attach` would keep refusing to pair panes long after the
  # window is gone.
  view_session_live() {
    local s n
    s=$(view_session_for "$1")
    tmux has-session -t "$s" 2>/dev/null || return 1
    n=$(tmux display-message -p -t "$s" '#{session_attached}' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    [ "${n:-0}" -gt 0 ]
  }
  
  # Every view session this script created, for teardown.
  view_sessions() {
    local names
    names=$(tmux list-sessions -F '#{session_name}' 2>/dev/null || true)
    # Tolerates the bare "<prefix>" form as well as "<prefix>-<window>": an older
    # run of this script used the unsuffixed name, and `down` must still reap it
    # rather than leave an orphan session holding the TUI alive.
    grep -E "^${VIEW_PREFIX}(-|\$)" <<< "$names" || true
  }
  
  gui_terminal() {
    [ "${REMOTE_CTRL_GUI:-1}" = 1 ] || return 1
    [ -n "${DISPLAY:-}" ] || [ -n "${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-}" ] || return 1
    local t
    for t in gnome-terminal x-terminal-emulator xterm konsole; do
      command -v "$t" > /dev/null && { printf '%s' "$t"; return 0; }
    done
    return 1
  }
  
  # start_bridge returns as soon as the bridge process exists, but deskmate-demo.sh
  # only creates the mimo window later: it first waits up to 30s for its ACP ready
  # file (deskmate-demo.sh:173) and opens the window at :184. Measured: without this
  # wait the window is not there yet, open_gui_view silently does nothing, and no
  # window ever appears. Waits slightly past that 30s deadline.
  wait_for_mimo_window() {
    # Nothing to wait for when no attach was requested — don't stall for 35s.
    { [ "$MIMO_ATTACH" = 1 ] && [ "$BACKEND" = "mimo" ]; } || return 1
  
    local i
    for i in $(seq 1 35); do
      mimo_window_exists && return 0
      sleep 1
    done
    warn "the mimo attach window never appeared within 35s"
    return 1
  }
  
  # Run outside tmux, deskmate-demo.sh pops a GNOME Terminal for `mimo attach`
  # (deskmate-demo.sh:99). We run it inside tmux, so it takes its other branch and
  # parks the TUI in a tmux window instead — which nobody sees until someone
  # attaches. Open one GUI window on that pane to restore the original feel.
  # open_gui_view <tmux-window> <window-title>
  #
  # Pops one GUI terminal showing that tmux window, so both halves of the PC side
  # are presented the same way DeskMate presented them: a real window each, not one
  # visible and one buried in a tmux session nobody attached.
  open_gui_view() {
    local win="$1" title="$2" term session cmd
    term=$(gui_terminal) || return 1
    window_exists "$win" || return 1
  
    # Already got a window on it — don't stack a second one.
    view_session_live "$win" && return 0
  
    session=$(view_session_for "$win")
    tmux has-session -t "$session" 2>/dev/null ||
      tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -t "$TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null ||
      return 1
  
    # Point this session at its window before attaching, rather than passing tmux a
    # `\;`-separated command list through another shell's quoting.
    tmux select-window -t "$session:$win" 2>/dev/null || true
  
    cmd="tmux attach -t $session"
    case "$term" in
      gnome-terminal)
        setsid "$term" --title="$title" -- bash -lc "$cmd" > /dev/null 2>&1 & ;;
      *)
        setsid "$term" -e bash -lc "$cmd" > /dev/null 2>&1 & ;;
    esac
    disown 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
  }
  
  # DeskMate showed two surfaces at once: the terminal you launched from kept the
  # bridge log and its `deskmate>` prompt (deskmate-demo.sh:216 parks it there with
  # `wait "$bridge_pid"`), and a separate GNOME Terminal ran `mimo attach`. Give
  # both the same treatment here — one window each — rather than one popped up and
  # the other hidden in a tmux session.
  #
  # Succeeds if at least one window opened.
  open_gui_views() {
    local opened=0 w
  
    gui_terminal > /dev/null || return 1
  
    # With `mimo attach` up, the agent's own TUI is where you actually work, so it
    # is the only window opened by default — the bridge log is diagnostics, kept one
    # command away (`log`) instead of in your face.
    #
    # Without attach it is the other way round: deskmate-demo.sh:143 refuses
    # --mimo-attach for any backend but mimo, so the bridge's `deskmate>` prompt is
    # then the ONLY interactive surface on this side and has to be the window.
    # The mimo window also arrives late, so wait for it rather than racing it.
    if wait_for_mimo_window; then
      open_gui_view "$MIMO_WINDOW" "remote-ctrl: mimo agent" && opened=1
    else
      w=$(bridge_window) &&
        open_gui_view "$w" "remote-ctrl: bridge (deskmate> prompt)" &&
        opened=1
    fi
  
    # Re-pin each window now that they all exist. deskmate-demo.sh:96 creates the
    # mimo window WITHOUT -d, so tmux selects it — and because these view sessions
    # are grouped, a session already parked on the bridge log gets dragged along.
    # Measured: both windows ended up showing the mimo TUI without this.
    pin_view_windows
    [ "$opened" = 1 ]
  }
  
  pin_view_windows() {
    local s w
    while IFS= read -r s; do
      [ -n "$s" ] || continue
      # Session name is "<prefix>-<window>", so the window is the trailing part.
      w="${s#"$VIEW_PREFIX"-}"
      [ "$w" = "$s" ] && continue
      window_exists "$w" || continue
      tmux select-window -t "$s:$w" 2>/dev/null || true
    done <<< "$(view_sessions)"
  }
  
  # deskmate-demo.sh keeps the bridge in the foreground of the window we start for
  # it, EXCEPT with --mimo-attach, where it relocates the bridge into its own
  # detached window (deskmate-demo.sh:171). Our own window is then just a launcher
  # holding a dead shell, so resolve whichever window actually carries the
  # `deskmate>` prompt instead of assuming one of the two.
  BRIDGE_LOG_WINDOW="deskmate-bridge"
  
  bridge_window() {
    window_exists "$BRIDGE_LOG_WINDOW" && { printf '%s' "$BRIDGE_LOG_WINDOW"; return 0; }
    window_exists bridge && { printf '%s' bridge; return 0; }
    return 1
  }
  
  bridge_pane_count() {
    local w
    w=$(bridge_window) || { printf '0'; return 0; }
    tmux list-panes -t "$TMUX_SESSION:$w" 2>/dev/null | wc -l
  }
  
  # Panes are addressed by their tmux pane id (%N), resolved from the command each
  # pane was started with. An index literal like `bridge.0` would be wrong on a
  # setup with `pane-base-index 1`, and once the mimo TUI is joined into this
  # window a wrong index would put keystrokes in the other program.
  pane_id_matching() {
    local needle="$1" window="$2" line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
      case "${line#* }" in *"$needle"*) printf '%s' "${line%% *}"; return 0 ;; esac
    done <<< "$(tmux list-panes -t "$TMUX_SESSION:$window" \
      -F '#{pane_id} #{pane_start_command}' 2>/dev/null)"
    return 1
  }
  
  # Either the relocated bridge process or the launcher that still fronts it; fall
  # back to the window's first pane. No pipe into head: same SIGPIPE reason.
  bridge_pane() {
    local w panes
    w=$(bridge_window) || return 1
    pane_id_matching 'deskmate-bridge.mjs' "$w" && return 0
    pane_id_matching 'deskmate-demo.sh' "$w" && return 0
    panes=$(tmux list-panes -t "$TMUX_SESSION:$w" -F '#{pane_id}' 2>/dev/null || true)
    printf '%s' "${panes%%$'\n'*}"
  }
  
  # The joined TUI pane: the one in this window that is not the bridge.
  mimo_pane_in_bridge_window() {
    local w panes line br
    w=$(bridge_window) || return 1
    br=$(bridge_pane)
    panes=$(tmux list-panes -t "$TMUX_SESSION:$w" -F '#{pane_id}' 2>/dev/null || true)
    while IFS= read -r line; do
      [ -n "$line" ] || continue
      [ "$line" = "$br" ] || { printf '%s' "$line"; return 0; }
    done <<< "$panes"
    return 1
  }
  
  # DeskMate let you watch the agent and the link at the same time. Same idea for
  # the PC half: bridge log left, mimo TUI right, one screen. Idempotent — a second
  # call finds the panes already joined.
  split_bridge_and_mimo() {
    local w
    w=$(bridge_window) || return 1
    if [ "$(bridge_pane_count)" -ge 2 ]; then
      return 0
    fi
    # join-pane destroys the window it takes the pane from, and that window is
    # exactly what the GUI view session is displaying. Stealing it would blank
    # someone's open window, so leave the panes alone while a window is really on
    # it — an orphaned view session (window closed) must not block this.
    view_session_live "$MIMO_WINDOW" && return 2
    mimo_window_exists || return 1
    tmux join-pane -h -l 50% -s "$TMUX_SESSION:$MIMO_WINDOW" -t "$TMUX_SESSION:$w" 2>/dev/null || return 1
    # The TUI is the interactive half here, so give it the keyboard.
    tmux select-pane -t "$(mimo_pane_in_bridge_window)" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
  }
  
  # `attach` means "show me the views again" — after closing a window, or from a
  # terminal that never had them. With a GUI it re-opens the same windows `up`
  # opened, which is idempotent. Without one (ssh, no DISPLAY) it falls back to
  # taking over this terminal, and only then does pane splitting make sense.
  do_attach() {
    tmux has-session -t "$TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null || die "nothing running; '$(basename "$0") up' first"
  
    if open_gui_views; then
      say "windows open: bridge log, and the mimo agent"
      say "the device console is not among them — that one is yours, on the device"
      return 0
    fi
  
    warn "no GUI terminal, so this terminal becomes the view"
    # 2 is "declined on purpose", distinct from 1 "nothing to pair with" — the two
    # deserve different explanations rather than one catch-all warning.
    local rc=0
    split_bridge_and_mimo || rc=$?
    case "$rc" in
      0)
        say "bridge log on the left, mimo TUI on the right (keyboard is on the TUI)"
        say "switch panes with Ctrl-b then o; detach with Ctrl-b then d" ;;
      2)
        say "the mimo TUI already has a window of its own, leaving it there" ;;
      *)
        warn "no $MIMO_WINDOW window to pair with (backend=$BACKEND, or mimo attach is off)" ;;
    esac
    sleep 1
    exec tmux attach -t "$TMUX_SESSION" \; select-window -t "$(bridge_window)"
  }
  
  do_mimo() {
    tmux has-session -t "$TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null || die "nothing running; '$(basename "$0") up' first"
    # If a no-GUI `attach` folded it into the bridge window, pull it back out so the
    # TUI gets a whole terminal again.
    local tui
    if ! mimo_window_exists && [ "$(bridge_pane_count)" -ge 2 ]; then
      tui=$(mimo_pane_in_bridge_window) &&
        tmux break-pane -d -s "$tui" -n "$MIMO_WINDOW" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    mimo_window_exists || die "no mimo TUI running; it needs backend=mimo with attach enabled"
  
    if open_gui_view "$MIMO_WINDOW" "remote-ctrl: mimo agent"; then
      say "the mimo agent window is open"
      return 0
    fi
  
    warn "no GUI terminal, so this terminal becomes the view"
    say "detach with Ctrl-b then d"
    sleep 1
    exec tmux attach -t "$TMUX_SESSION" \; select-window -t "$MIMO_WINDOW"
  }
  
  do_down() {
    # The emulator is deliberately left alone: this script never started it, and
    # killing someone else's device out from under them is not its business.
    say "stopping the bridge"
    pkill -f "[d]eskmate-bridge.mjs" 2>/dev/null || true
    # Only ever the demo's own broker: matching the config path leaves the
    # system broker on 1883 alone.
    if [ -f "$BROKER_CONF" ]; then
      pkill -f "mosquitto -c $BROKER_CONF" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    pkill -x mosquitto_sub 2>/dev/null || true
    # Grouped sessions share their windows, and a window outlives the kill of any
    # single session in the group — measured: killing one leaves the other, with
    # the pane's process still running. So the view session has to go first, or
    # `down` would leave the mimo TUI and its GUI terminal behind.
    local s
    while IFS= read -r s; do
      [ -n "$s" ] || continue
      tmux kill-session -t "$s" 2>/dev/null || true
    done <<< "$(view_sessions)"
    tmux kill-session -t "$TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -f "$CRED_FILE"
    restore_config
    unstage_sources
    say "stopped. The built image stays in $BUILD_DIR"
  }
  
  case "${1:-}" in
    build) do_build ;;
    up) do_up ;;
    verify) do_verify ;;
    attach) do_attach ;;
    mimo) do_mimo ;;
    status) do_status ;;
    wire) do_wire ;;
    broker) start_broker ;;
    bridge) ensure_session; start_bridge ;;
    device) device_instructions ;;
    down) do_down ;;
    ""|-h|--help|help) usage ;;
    *) printf 'unknown command: %s\n\n' "$1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac

input.new_string:
check_broker() {
  command -v mosquitto_pub > /dev/null || { warn "mosquitto_pub absent, skipping the broker probe"; return 0; }
  if broker_reachable; then
    say "broker reachable at $HOST_ADDRESS:$BROKER_PORT"
    return 0
  fi

  # "with the supplied credentials" is the wrong thing to say when none were
  # supplied — it sends you looking for a wrong password instead of an unset
  # variable. Name which of the three it actually is.
  local err
  err=$(timeout 5 mosquitto_pub -h "$HOST_ADDRESS" -p "$BROKER_PORT" \
    ${MQTT_USERNAME:+-u "$MQTT_USERNAME"} ${MQTT_PASSWORD:+-P "$MQTT_PASSWORD"} \
    -t "$TOPIC_PREFIX/_probe" -m probe 2>&1 || true)

  if [ -z "$MQTT_USERNAME" ] && [ -z "$MQTT_PASSWORD" ]; then
    warn "no broker credentials in this shell, and $HOST_ADDRESS:$BROKER_PORT refuses anonymous clients"
    warn "'export' only lives in the terminal you typed it in, so run this here first:"
    warn "  export DESKMATE_MQTT_USERNAME=... DESKMATE_MQTT_PASSWORD=..."
  elif grep -qi 'not authorised' <<< "$err"; then
    warn "the broker rejected user '$MQTT_USERNAME' at $HOST_ADDRESS:$BROKER_PORT"
    warn "the connection worked, so this is the username or password, not the address"
  else
    warn "cannot reach $HOST_ADDRESS:$BROKER_PORT at all:"
    printf '%s\n' "${err:-(no output from mosquitto_pub)}" >&2
    warn "check REMOTE_CTRL_HOST_ADDRESS, or run '$(basename "$0") broker' for a local one"
  fi
  die "broker check failed"
}

你现在只需要在要跑 `up` 的那个终端里补上:


凭据本身是对的——我实测 `deskmate/5006` 在 `127.0.0.1` 和 `10.189.140.244` 上都发布成功,broker 也在跑(`0.0.0.0:1883`),IP 仍是 `10.189.140.244`。纯粹是新终端没继承 `export`。

嫌每次敲麻烦的话,写个 0600 的文件 source 它:

```bash
umask 077; cat > ~/.remote-ctrl-env <<'EOF'
export DESKMATE_MQTT_USERNAME=deskmate
export DESKMATE_MQTT_PASSWORD=5006
EOF
# 之后每个新终端:
. ~/.remote-ctrl-env
```

## 第一段的真问题

`summary` 被当成流式文本在用。bridge 每次快照都塞一份当前截断后的 summary,设备侧 `remote_ctrl_channel.c:69` 原样打一行。于是一个 turn 里滚出好几行各自截断的片段,看着像一份残缺的抄本——但它其实是状态行的连续快照。

`程和专业任务。` 那行不是接着上一行,是**后一个快照**的 summary 恰好是当时文本的尾部。

改法在设备侧:给 STATE 行加个前缀标明它是状态,比如 `status: ...`,让人一眼看出不该当抄本读;流式内容本来就该去 `remote_output` 看。

## 第二段的真问题

这个更实在,是我代码的问题。`remote_link.c:308`:

```c
snprintf(link->summary, sizeof(link->summary), "%s: %s", tool_call_id, status);
```

把裸 ACP tool call id 当摘要输出,于是你看到 `tooluse_m7MqB5bPlKuDegoWjm6j38: completed`——人读不出任何信息。而真正有用的 `bash` / `Delete /tmp/1.txt` 在前面两行,是独立快照,和结果行没有任何关联。

改完并重编验证了。

## 改了什么

**工具调用那三行**。根因是 `remote_link.c` 拿裸 ACP id 当摘要,而人能读的名字(`bash` / `Delete /tmp/1.txt`)在**另外的快照**里,设备侧无法可靠地把两者配对。所以让 bridge 把 title 随结果一起发过来(`bridge-core.js:351` 加 `title` 字段,用它自己的 `summarizeMessage` 界定长度),设备侧渲染成:

```
tool 'Delete /tmp/1.txt' completed
```

没有 title 时(旧 bridge)退回用 id,不会失效。

**流式回复那几行**。它们其实是 bridge 的**状态行**快照,不是抄本——完整回复一直在 transcript 里,`remote_output` 能取回。那个 `…` 来自 bridge 的 `utf8Summary()`,是对状态行的有意截断。现在加了 `status:` 前缀,一眼能看出不该当抄本读。

顺带修了一个会撕行的问题:title 里的控制字符(换行、tab)会把一行 syslog 撕成好几行,现在压平成空格。这里有个坑我特意绕开了——压平必须在**比较之前**做,否则存的是压平版、进来的是原始版,`strcmp` 每次都判"变了",反而把刷屏放大。

host 测试 5 组全过(新增了 title、空 title 回退、控制字符压平三组断言),bridge 测试 37/37。镜像 14:29:19 重编成功,四个对象都在 14:28:4x 重编过,新格式字符串 `tool '%s' %s` / `status: %s` 都在 ELF 里。

镜像里还剩 2 处 `%s: %s` 是别的模块的,我的源码里已经没有。

**bridge 也要重启**——`bridge-core.js` 改了,但正在跑的那个 node 进程还是旧代码,不会发 title。所以:

```bash
rc down      # 顺带还原代码树(现在 stage 了 15 个文件)
```

input.new_string:
# What this demo image needs, as "<symbol>=<value>"; "=n" disables a symbol.
#
# WEIXIN is off because it is `default y` in Kconfig and, with no token
# configured, its channel logs "No token, waiting..." every 5 seconds
# (weixin_channel.c:321) — which buries the remote_ctrl lines you are here to
# read. Nothing in this feature touches it, and weixin_channel.h carries inline
# stubs for the disabled case, so the call sites in agent_main.c still compile.
# Set REMOTE_CTRL_KEEP_WEIXIN=1 to leave it on.
demo_config_changes() {
  printf '%s\n' 'CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REMOTE_CTRL=y'
  [ "${REMOTE_CTRL_KEEP_WEIXIN:-0}" = 1 ] || printf '%s\n' 'CONFIG_AI_AGENT_WEIXIN=n'
}

# Rewrites one symbol, dropping whichever form of it is already there. A bool
# set to n is written as "# SYMBOL is not set", the only spelling Kconfig reads
# back as n; a plain "SYMBOL=n" line would be ignored and the `default y` would
# quietly win.
apply_config() {
  local symbol="$1" value="$2" line

  if [ "$value" = "n" ]; then

    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$DEFCONFIG.tmp"

    awk -v new="$line" '

      { print }
      END { if (!inserted) print new }
    ' "$DEFCONFIG.tmp" > "$DEFCONFIG.tmp2"
    mv "$DEFCONFIG.tmp2" "$DEFCONFIG.tmp"
  fi

  mv "$DEFCONFIG.tmp" "$DEFCONFIG"
  grep -qxF "$line" "$DEFCONFIG" || die "failed to apply $line"
}

enable_config() {

  # Back up before the first edit, never after: the copy is what `down` restores
  # byte for byte, and this file routinely carries uncommitted local edits.
  [ -f "$DEFCONFIG_BACKUP" ] || cp -p "$DEFCONFIG" "$DEFCONFIG_BACKUP"

  while IFS= read -r change; do
    [ -n "$change" ] || continue
    symbol="${change%%=*}"
    value="${change#*=}"
    apply_config "$symbol" "$value"
  done <<< "$(demo_config_changes)"

  say "board config prepared (backup at $DEFCONFIG_BACKUP)"
}

# What this demo image needs, one "<symbol>=<value>" per line; "=n" disables.
#
# WEIXIN is turned off because it is `default y` in Kconfig and, with no token
# configured, its channel logs "No token, waiting..." every five seconds
# (weixin_channel.c:321) straight into the console you are reading remote_ctrl
# on. Nothing in this feature uses it, and weixin_channel.h ships inline stubs
# for the disabled case so the call sites in agent_main.c still compile. Set
# REMOTE_CTRL_KEEP_WEIXIN=1 to leave it enabled.
demo_config_changes() {
  printf '%s\n' 'CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REMOTE_CTRL=y'
  [ "${REMOTE_CTRL_KEEP_WEIXIN:-0}" = 1 ] || printf '%s\n' 'CONFIG_AI_AGENT_WEIXIN=n'
}

# Rewrites one symbol, dropping whichever spelling of it is already present.
#
# A bool turned off must be written as "# SYMBOL is not set" — that is the only
# form Kconfig reads back as n. A literal "SYMBOL=n" line is ignored, so the
# Kconfig `default y` would quietly win and the symbol would still be on.
apply_config() {
  local symbol="$1" value="$2" line

  if [ "$value" = "n" ]; then
    line="# $symbol is not set"
  else
    line="$symbol=$value"
  fi

  grep -qxF "$line" "$DEFCONFIG" && return 0

  # Remove both spellings so the two can never sit in the file fighting. The
  # anchored "=" / " is not set" stops SYMBOL from also matching SYMBOL_SUFFIX.
  grep -vE "^(# )?${symbol}( is not set$|=)" "$DEFCONFIG" > "$DEFCONFIG.tmp"

  if [ "$value" = "n" ]; then
    # A "# ... is not set" line has no place in the alphabetical run; Kconfig
    # does not care about order, so append it.
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$DEFCONFIG.tmp"
  else
    # defconfig is savedefconfig output, so keep the sorted run sorted.
    awk -v new="$line" '
      !inserted && /^CONFIG_/ && $0 > new { print new; inserted = 1 }
      { print }
      END { if (!inserted) print new }
    ' "$DEFCONFIG.tmp" > "$DEFCONFIG.tmp2"
    mv "$DEFCONFIG.tmp2" "$DEFCONFIG.tmp"
  fi

  mv "$DEFCONFIG.tmp" "$DEFCONFIG"
  grep -qxF "$line" "$DEFCONFIG" || die "failed to apply: $line"
  say "  config: $line"
}

# The board defconfig is shared and routinely carries uncommitted local edits,
# so it is restored from an exact byte copy. `git checkout` would silently throw
# those edits away.
enable_config() {
  local change symbol value

  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  # Back up before the first edit, never after — this copy is what `down`
  # restores byte for byte.
  [ -f "$DEFCONFIG_BACKUP" ] || cp -p "$DEFCONFIG" "$DEFCONFIG_BACKUP"

  # Every change is applied every time. An early "already enabled" return here
  # would skip the rest of the list on a tree where the first symbol was already
  # set, silently dropping the others.
  while IFS= read -r change; do
    [ -n "$change" ] || continue
    symbol="${change%%=*}"
    value="${change#*=}"
    apply_config "$symbol" "$value"
  done <<< "$(demo_config_changes)"

  say "board config prepared (backup at $DEFCONFIG_BACKUP)"
}

input.new_string:
# True when the configured build tree already carries every change we want.
#
# This has to be asked, because nothing else will: build.ninja has no edge from
# the board defconfig to the generated .config, so once a build directory is
# configured its .config is frozen and later defconfig edits are silently
# ignored. Measured: a .config dated a day earlier than the defconfig, with
# CONFIG_AI_AGENT_WEIXIN=y despite the defconfig disabling it.
config_matches_image() {
  local config="$root_dir/$BUILD_DIR/.config" change symbol value

  [ -f "$config" ] || return 1

  while IFS= read -r change; do
    [ -n "$change" ] || continue
    symbol="${change%%=*}"
    value="${change#*=}"
    if [ "$value" = "n" ]; then
      grep -q "^${symbol}=y" "$config" && return 1
    else
      grep -q "^${symbol}=${value}" "$config" || return 1
    fi
  done <<< "$(demo_config_changes)"

  return 0
}

# build.sh:113 says it plainly: under cmake there is no distclean, you delete the
# binary directory. That is the only way to make a defconfig change take effect.
reconfigure_build_dir() {
  local out="$root_dir/$BUILD_DIR"

  # Refuse to delete anything that is not recognisably a cmake build tree, so a
  # mistyped REMOTE_CTRL_BUILD_DIR cannot take a source directory with it.
  [ -f "$out/CMakeCache.txt" ] ||
    die "$BUILD_DIR has no CMakeCache.txt; refusing to delete it"

  warn "the board config changed, so $BUILD_DIR must be reconfigured"
  warn "cmake has no distclean: this deletes the build tree and rebuilds in full"
  rm -rf "$out"
}

do_build() {
  command -v cmake > /dev/null || die "cmake not found"
  stage_sources
  enable_config

  if [ -d "$root_dir/$BUILD_DIR" ] && ! config_matches_image; then
    reconfigure_build_dir
  fi

  say "building $BOARD_CONFIG into $BUILD_DIR (a few minutes)"
  ( cd "$root_dir" && ./build.sh "$BOARD_CONFIG/" --cmake -b "$BUILD_DIR" -j"$(nproc)" )
  assert_image
  say "build done. Next: $(basename "$0") up"
}

weixin 关掉了,但过程中挖出一个**比它严重得多的问题**,得先说这个。

## 陈旧 `.config`:defconfig 改动一直是空操作

我加的那条 weixin 断言当场抓到:编译"成功"了,但生成的 `.config` 里 `CONFIG_AI_AGENT_WEIXIN` 仍是 `y`。查下去发现 `.config` 的 mtime 是 **9-01 16:03**,而 defconfig 是今天 15:00 改的——`build.ninja` 里**没有** defconfig → `.config` 的依赖边,构建目录一旦配置过,`.config` 就冻住了。

含意:**自 9-01 16:03 以来,我所有的 defconfig 改动都没生效过**。之前"config on"能通过断言,只是因为 `REMOTE_CTRL=y` 早就烧进那份旧 `.config` 里了,不是因为我改对了。源码改动是真生效的(对象文件确实在重编),所以上一轮的日志格式修复没问题。

`build.sh:113-114` 自己写着答案:cmake 下没有 distclean,要重新配置就删构建目录。脚本现在会比对期望配置与实际 `.config`,不一致就删掉重建(删之前检查 `CMakeCache.txt` 存在,防止 `REMOTE_CTRL_BUILD_DIR` 打错把源码目录删了)。代价是全量编译:这次 4041 个目标、4 分 38 秒,而不是增量的 30 秒。

## 验证结果

```
.config   : 2026-09-02 15:11:21   (不再是 9-01 的陈旧文件)
# CONFIG_AI_AGENT_WEIXIN is not set
weixin_channel.c.o : 0 个          (真的没编进去)
remote 对象        : 6 个
"No token, waiting..." : ELF 里 0 处   ← 刷屏源已从镜像里消失
"tool '%s' %s" : 1 处 / "status: %s" : 2 处   ← 上一轮的修复仍在
```

顺带说一个 Kconfig 陷阱:bool 关掉必须写 `# SYMBOL is not set`,写 `SYMBOL=n` 会被忽略、`default y` 照样赢。所以断言是对**生成的 `.config`** 做的,不是对我改的 defconfig——否则就是自己检查自己。

先答你的问题,再说命名。

## 这四个是什么

`remote_output` 就是你刚才那个"拼不起来"问题的答案。它打印**完整的回复抄本**——设备侧一直完整保存着,`status:` 那些行只是 bridge 的状态行快照(有界、会截断),不是抄本。你看到的碎片是状态行,完整内容一直在,用这个命令取。

`remote_usage` 发一个只读的用量查询,刷新计费数字(就是那行 `Billing: / 18247 tokens`)。

`remote_once` / `remote_deny` 是人工批准/拒绝远端 agent 的工具调用请求。这两个**永远不会注册成 LLM 可调用的工具**——批准是人的行为,模型若能同时请求又批准,权限模型就是装饰。

## 命名确实该统一

## Goal

把 `contest2026_272_tokenwujixian` 的板上 app `app/deskmate` 转成 `packages/ai_agent` 的一个 feature——远程控制(remote control),设备作为客户端连接远端跑 ACP 的 agent(mimocode / kiro-cli)。当前阶段:PC 侧一键脚本已落到团队仓库并对齐 deskmate 的呈现方式;正在打磨设备侧的日志可读性与命令命名。

**用户最后一问尚未回答**:`remote_output` / `remote_usage` / `remote_once` / `remote_deny` 各自作用是什么,`remote_output` 能干什么,以及为什么不把这些也统一成 `rxxx` 短名(承接刚做完的 `remote_ask` → `rask`)。

## Instructions

- **权限决策只允许人工**:`remote_once` / `remote_deny` 只能从 NSH 命令(及将来 GPIO 按键)触达,**绝不注册为 LLM 可调用的 tool**。代码注释和 tool description 都要钉住这条。
- **链路形态**:保留 DeskMate Link(设备 —MQTT→ PC bridge —stdio→ ACP agent),不做设备直连 ACP。
- **代码落地**:`packages/ai_agent` 本地 feature 分支,Kconfig `default n`,不推 upstream。
- **PC / 设备分工是硬边界**(用户明确纠正过两次):PC 侧脚本只管 broker + bridge + mimo attach 窗口;**设备侧由用户自己操作**——启模拟器、`ai_agent`、`set_remote_auth`、`set_remote`、所有 `remote_*` 命令。脚本绝不用 `send-keys` 驱动设备控制台。
- **脚本位置**:团队仓库 `tools/acp-bridge/bin/remote-ctrl-demo.sh`,与 `deskmate-demo.sh` 并列(worktree 里那份已删,只有一份)。
- **呈现要对齐 deskmate**:有 `mimo attach` 时只弹 agent TUI 窗口(那是实际工作的地方),`deskmate>` 降级为按需的 `log` 子命令。
- **避免冗余**:命令表不要两个名字做一件事(用户否掉了 `rask` + `remote_ask` 双名,已删长名);设备 `help` 已有的内容不要在 PC 脚本里重复。
- **凭据只走环境变量**(`DESKMATE_MQTT_USERNAME` / `DESKMATE_MQTT_PASSWORD`),不放命令行。真实默认值:`mqtt://10.189.140.244:1883`、`deskmate` / `5006`、`goldfish-1`、backend mimo、`--mimo-attach --mimo-attach-port 4096`。
- ai_agent 的 Ctrl-C 缺陷**用户明确说先不管**。

## Discoveries

**架构判断**:ACP 的设计前提(稳定 stdio 管道、无界消息、阻塞式双向)与跑在 WiFi 上的受限设备三条全冲。`mcp_client.c`(纯出向)、`mcp_server.c`(同步应答、仅 stdio)、`node_client.c`(从不回复入向)三种既有形状都不满足 ACP 需要的「双向 peer + 待答入向请求表」。Link 正是那层适配。`kiro-cli acp` 只有 stdio、无监听参数。

**★ 陈旧 `.config`:defconfig 改动长期是空操作(本轮最重要的发现)**。`build.ninja` 里**没有** defconfig → `.config` 的依赖边(只有反方向的 `savedefconfig` phony target),构建目录一旦配置过 `.config` 就冻住。实测:`.config` mtime 停在 9-01 16:03,而 defconfig 是 9-02 15:00 改的,`CONFIG_AI_AGENT_WEIXIN=y` 仍在。**含意:自 9-01 16:03 起所有 defconfig 改动都没生效**;之前 "config on" 能通过断言只因为 `REMOTE_CTRL=y` 早烧进旧 `.config`。源码改动是生效的(对象文件确实重编)。`build.sh:113-114` 自己写着解法:cmake 下没有 distclean,要重配就删构建目录。已修:`config_matches_image()` 比对期望配置与实际 `.config`,不一致就 `rm -rf`(删前检查 `CMakeCache.txt` 存在,防 `REMOTE_CTRL_BUILD_DIR` 打错删源码)。代价:全量编译 4041 目标 / 4分38秒,而非增量 30 秒。

**Kconfig 陷阱**:bool 关掉必须写 `# SYMBOL is not set`,写 `SYMBOL=n` 会被忽略、`default y` 照样赢。所以断言必须对**生成的 `.config`** 做,不能对自己改的 defconfig 做。

**`mimo acp --port N` 是 bind 语义**,不是连已有实例(拿 4187 起探针验证了 LISTEN)。`deskmate-bridge.mjs:51` 把 `["acp","--port",N]` 传给 adapter,所以 bridge 会 bind 4096——而**这台机器上 4096 被承载本会话的宿主 mimo(pid 因重启而变)占着,绝不能碰**。已加端口预检自动往后挪(实测挪到 4097,两者共存)。`port_free` 正则要求端口号前紧贴 `:` 或 `.`,因为真实 `ss -ltn` 里有大量 Send-Q 恰好是 4096 的行。

命名统一了,顺带修掉一个真 bug:help 块上一轮已经改成短名,但 `nsh_commands.c` 的分发还认长名,所以 `rstat` / `rreply` / `rusage` / `ronce` / `rdeny` 敲下去全部落到 unknown command——六个命令里只有 `rask` 是通的。现在六个短名 help 与分发一一对上。

改动落点:

- `nsh_commands.c:1013-1029` 分发改短名,合并成一条说明「每个动作只有一个拼写」的注释
- `cmd_channel.c` 待批准提示 → `'ronce'` / `'rdeny'`;用量查询回执 → `'rstat'`
- `remote_ctrl_channel.c:331` → `Prompt sent. Use 'rstat' for progress and 'rreply' for the full reply.`;`:73` 那条解释 status 行为何是碎片的注释也改指 `rreply`
- `Kconfig:199-201` 帮助文本列出 r* 命令
- 脚本三处:设备指引、fake 后端批准步骤、以及 `verify` 的镜像 marker

`set_remote` / `set_remote_auth` 保持原名(仓库通用的 `set_<thing>` 配置命名),两个 LLM 工具 `remote_agent_prompt` / `remote_agent_status` 也没动——那是 tool registry 的命名空间,和控制台命令不是一套。

一个维护陷阱值得记一下:脚本 `verify` 断言的是设备里一条**精确的字符串**(原来是 `Prompt sent. Use remote_status`)。改设备侧文案必须同步改 marker,否则 `verify` 会假失败。这次是一起改的。

验证:host 协议测试 5 组全过;`bash -n` 通过;镜像重编成功(40 秒增量,配置未变故未触发重配);ELF 串校验六个短名各有 1 处独立分发字面量 + 6 条 help 行,用户可见的长名 0 处(残留的 3 处 `remote_output` 是 C 函数符号 `cmd_remote_output`,内部名,按之前的约定保留);`packages/ai_agent` 里 24 个 staged 文件与 worktree 逐字节一致。

还没解决的是 `verify` 误报设备未连接那条——设备空闲时应用层完全静默,观测窗口内本就可能没有出向流量,那个判据本身站不住。需要改成看 bridge→device 的 snapshot 是否被接受,或者在观测期引导操作一次。要现在动它吗?

dev2br=$(grep -cF 'device-to-bridge' <<< "$traffic" || true)
  br2dev=$(grep -cF 'bridge-to-device' <<< "$traffic" || true)

  # Each direction is split out once and matched from that cache. Chaining
  # `grep dir | grep -q type` would let the reader exit on its first hit and
  # SIGPIPE the writer; `set -o pipefail` then reports 141 and the type is
  # silently dropped from the report even though it was on the wire. Measured
  # at 141 on a large capture, so this is the busy-link case, not a corner one.
  local outbound inbound
  outbound=$(grep -F 'device-to-bridge' <<< "$traffic" || true)
  inbound=$(grep -F 'bridge-to-device' <<< "$traffic" || true)

  # The link test. An idle device sends nothing at all: it publishes on connect
  # and on user action, and has no application-level heartbeat (only MQTT
  # keepalive, which stays inside the broker and is invisible here). So counting
  # device-to-bridge messages reports a healthy idle device as absent.
  #
  # A snapshot is the signal that works instead. bridge-core.js returns early
  # from snapshot() unless linkActive && nonce hold, and both are set only by a
  # hello that passed validation, so a snapshot carrying a connection_nonce
  # means the bridge is holding an established session. deskmate-bridge.mjs
  # beats one out every 10s, so it arrives whether or not the device speaks.
  local snapshots nonces handshook=0
  snapshots=$(grep -cF '"type":"snapshot"' <<< "$inbound" || true)
  nonces=$(grep -oE '"connection_nonce":"[^"]+"' <<< "$inbound" |
             sed 's/.*:"//; s/"$//' | sort -u || true)
  if [ "$snapshots" -gt 0 ] && [ -n "$nonces" ]; then handshook=1; fi

  printf '\n'
  say "bridge -> device : $br2dev message(s), $snapshots snapshot(s)"
  say "device -> bridge : $dev2br message(s) (an idle device is silent by design)"
  printf '\n'

input.description: Test verify decision logic with synthetic traffic
input.command:
cd /tmp && cat > rc_verify_logic.sh <<'OUTER'
set -euo pipefail
say()  { printf '>> %s\n' "$1"; }
warn() { printf '!! %s\n' "$1" >&2; }
device_instructions() { printf '(device instructions)\n'; }

judge() {
  local traffic="$1"
  local outbound inbound dev2br br2dev
  outbound=$(grep -F 'device-to-bridge' <<< "$traffic" || true)
  inbound=$(grep -F 'bridge-to-device' <<< "$traffic" || true)
  dev2br=$(grep -c . <<< "$outbound" || true)
  br2dev=$(grep -c . <<< "$inbound" || true)

  local snapshots nonces handshook=0
  snapshots=$(grep -cF '"type":"snapshot"' <<< "$inbound" || true)
  nonces=$(grep -oE '"connection_nonce":"[^"]+"' <<< "$inbound" | sed 's/.*:"//; s/"$//' | sort -u || true)
  if [ "$snapshots" -gt 0 ] && [ -n "$nonces" ]; then handshook=1; fi

  say "bridge -> device : $br2dev message(s), $snapshots snapshot(s)"
  say "device -> bridge : $dev2br message(s) (an idle device is silent by design)"

  if [ "$handshook" -eq 0 ]; then
    if [ "$br2dev" -eq 0 ] && [ "$dev2br" -eq 0 ]; then
      warn "nothing on the wire at all"
    elif [ "$br2dev" -gt 0 ]; then
      warn "the bridge published, but no snapshot: it is holding no session"
    else
      warn "the device published, but the bridge never snapshotted back"
    fi
    return 1
  fi
  local sessions
  sessions=$(printf '%s\n' "$nonces" | grep -c . || true)
  say "established session ($snapshots snapshot(s))"
  if [ "$sessions" -gt 1 ]; then say "  $sessions distinct nonces: re-handshook"; fi
  return 0
}

P=deskmate/goldfish-1
run() { printf '\n--- %s ---\n' "$1"; shift; judge "$1" && echo "VERDICT: pass(0)" || echo "VERDICT: fail($?)"; }

run "A: total silence" ""
run "B: idle device, bridge snapshotting (THE REGRESSION CASE)" \
"$P/bridge-to-device {\"v\":1,\"type\":\"snapshot\",\"connection_nonce\":\"abc\",\"seq\":1}
$P/bridge-to-device {\"v\":1,\"type\":\"snapshot\",\"connection_nonce\":\"abc\",\"seq\":2}"
run "C: bridge talks, no session (hello_ack/error only)" \
"$P/bridge-to-device {\"v\":1,\"type\":\"error\",\"error\":\"hello required\"}"
run "D: device talks, bridge silent" \
"$P/device-to-bridge {\"cmd\":\"hello\",\"connection_nonce\":\"xyz\"}"
run "E: full healthy exchange" \
"$P/device-to-bridge {\"cmd\":\"hello\",\"connection_nonce\":\"abc\"}
$P/bridge-to-device {\"v\":1,\"type\":\"hello_ack\",\"connection_nonce\":\"abc\"}
$P/bridge-to-device {\"v\":1,\"type\":\"snapshot\",\"connection_nonce\":\"abc\",\"seq\":1}"

# Nonces are read off the snapshot lines only, not all inbound traffic:

  local snapshot_lines snapshots nonces handshook=0

  snapshots=$(grep -c . <<< "$snapshot_lines" || true)
  nonces=$(grep -oE '"connection_nonce":"[^"]+"' <<< "$snapshot_lines" |
             sed 's/.*:"//; s/"$//' | sort -u || true)
  if [ "$snapshots" -gt 0 ] && [ -n "$nonces" ]; then handshook=1; fi

input.new_string:
# 0 = the bridge holds a connection to the broker, 1 = it does not, 2 = unknown.
#
# A live bridge process is not the same thing as a bridge on the broker: if its
# connection dropped it publishes nothing, which looks exactly like an absent
# device from the wire. Without this the failure path would send you to the
# device console to debug a PC-side problem.
bridge_on_broker() {
  command -v ss > /dev/null || return 2

  local pids sockets pid
  pids=$(pgrep -f "[d]eskmate-bridge.mjs" || true)
  [ -n "$pids" ] || return 1

  # Cached, then matched from a here-string: `ss | grep -q` lets grep exit first
  # and SIGPIPE ss, which pipefail then reports as a failure.
  sockets=$(ss -tnp 2>/dev/null || true)
  [ -n "$sockets" ] || return 2

  # The port is anchored to the peer column, immediately before `users:`. A bare
  # `:$port` also matches a Send-Q that happens to equal the port number.
  while IFS= read -r pid; do
    [ -n "$pid" ] || continue
    if grep -qE "^ESTAB.*:${BROKER_PORT}[[:space:]]+users:\(\(\"[^\"]+\",pid=${pid}," \
         <<< "$sockets"; then
      return 0
    fi
  done <<< "$pids"
  return 1
}

do_verify() {
  command -v mosquitto_sub > /dev/null || die "mosquitto_sub not installed"
  pgrep -f "[d]eskmate-bridge.mjs" > /dev/null ||
    die "the bridge is not running; '$(basename "$0") up' first"
